sanskrit: prāptarājyasya rāmasya rākṣasānāṃ vadhe kṛte ājagmur ṛṣayaḥ sarve rāghavaṃ pratinanditum
english: After Rāma had obtained his kingdom and the slaughter of the rākṣasas had been accomplished, all the sages came to pay homage to the Rāghava.

sanskrit: kauśiko 'tha yavakrīto raibhyaś cyavana eva ca kaṇvo medhātitheḥ putraḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ye śritāḥ
english: Kauśika, Yavakrīta, Raibhya, Cyavana, and Kaṇva the son of Medhātithi — those who dwelt in the eastern quarter came.

sanskrit: svastyātreyaś ca bhagavān namuciḥ pramucus tathā ājagmus te sahāgastyā ye śritā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: The venerable Svastyātreya, Namuci, Pramucu, and those who dwelt in the southern quarter came together with Agastya.

sanskrit: pṛṣadguḥ kavaṣo dhaumyo raudreyaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ te 'py ājagmuḥ saśiṣyā vai ye śritāḥ paścimāṃ diśam
english: Pṛṣadgu, Kavaṣa, Dhaumya, and the great sage Raudreya — those who dwelt in the western quarter also came with their disciples.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaḥ kaśyapo 'thātrir viśvāmitro 'tha gautamaḥ jamadagnir bharadvājas te 'pi saptamaharṣayaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Gautama, Jamadagni, and Bharadvāja — these seven great seers also came.

sanskrit: saṃprāpyaite mahātmāno rāghavasya niveśanam viṣṭhitāḥ pratihārārthaṃ hutāśanasamaprabhāḥ
english: These great-souled ones, blazing like sacrificial fire, arrived at the dwelling of the Rāghava and stationed themselves at the gate, awaiting admission.

sanskrit: pratihāras tatas tūrṇam agastyavacanād atha samīpaṃ rāghavasyāśu praviveśa mahātmanaḥ
english: Then the gatekeeper, at Agastya's word, quickly entered the presence of the great-souled Rāghava.

sanskrit: sa rāmaṃ dṛśya sahasā pūrṇacandrasamadyutim agastyaṃ kathayām āsa saṃprātam ṛṣibhiḥ saha
english: Seeing Rāma, whose radiance was like the full moon, he announced to him the arrival of Agastya together with the sages.

sanskrit: śrutvā prāptān munīṃs tāṃs tu bālasūryasamaprabhān tadovāca nṛpo dvāḥsthaṃ praveśaya yathāsukham
english: Hearing that those sages, whose brilliance was like the rising sun, had arrived, the king said to the doorkeeper: "Admit them at their ease."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā prāptān munīṃs tāṃs tu pratyutthāya kṛtāñjaliḥ rāmo 'bhivādya prayata āsanāny ādideśa ha
english: Seeing those sages who had come, Rāma rose to receive them with joined palms, greeted them reverently, and with a purified mind directed them to seats.

sanskrit: teṣu kāñcanacitreṣu svāstīrṇeṣu sukheṣu ca yathārham upaviṣṭās te āsaneṣv ṛṣipuṃgavāḥ
english: Those foremost sages seated themselves appropriately upon the well-spread, comfortable, gold-ornamented thrones.

sanskrit: rāmeṇa kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭāḥ saśiṣyāḥ sapurogamāḥ maharṣayo vedavido rāmaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Asked after their welfare by Rāma, those great sages, knowers of the Vedas, together with their disciples and attendants, spoke these words to Rāma.

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ no mahābāho sarvatra raghunandana tvāṃ tu diṣṭyā kuśalinaṃ paśyāmo hataśātravam
english: "We are well in all respects, O mighty-armed one, O delight of the Raghus. By good fortune we see you well, with your enemies slain."

sanskrit: na hi bhāraḥ sa te rāma rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ sadhanus tvaṃ hi lokāṃs trīn vijayethā na saṃśayaḥ
english: "For Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, was no burden to you, O Rāma; armed with your bow you could conquer the three worlds — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvayā hato rāma rāvaṇaḥ putrapautravān diṣṭyā vijayinaṃ tvādya paśyāmaḥ saha bhāryayā
english: "By good fortune, O Rāma, you have slain Rāvaṇa together with his sons and grandsons. By good fortune we see you today victorious together with your wife."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā prahasto vikaṭo virūpākṣo mahodaraḥ akampanaś ca durdharṣo nihatās te niśācarāḥ
english: "By good fortune, Prahasta, Vikaṭa, Virūpākṣa, Mahodara, and the formidable Akampana — those night-roaming rākṣasas have been slain by you."

sanskrit: yasya pramāṇād vipulaṃ pramāṇaṃ neha vidyate diṣṭyā te samare rāma kumbhakarṇo nipātitaḥ
english: "He of whose vast measure there is none mightier in this world — by good fortune, O Rāma, Kumbhakarṇa has been felled by you in battle."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvaṃ rākṣasendreṇa dvandvayuddham upāgataḥ devatānām avadhyena vijayaṃ prāptavān asi
english: "By good fortune you engaged the lord of rākṣasas in single combat and have won victory over one who was unkillable by the gods."

sanskrit: saṃkhye tasya na kiṃ cit tu rāvaṇasya parābhavaḥ dvandvayuddham anuprāpto diṣṭyā te rāvaṇir hataḥ
english: "The defeat of Rāvaṇa in battle was nothing; it was when single combat came that the feat mattered — by good fortune Rāvaṇa's son Indrajit has been slain by you."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tasya mahābāho kālasyevābhidhāvataḥ muktaḥ suraripor vīra prāptaś ca vijayas tvayā
english: "By good fortune, O mighty-armed hero, you were freed from that foe of the gods who rushed at you like Death himself, and victory has been attained by you."

sanskrit: vismayas tv eṣa naḥ saumya saṃśrutyendrajitaṃ hatam avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ mahāmāyādharo yudhi
english: "Yet this is our wonder, O gentle one, upon hearing that Indrajit has been slain — he who was unkillable by all living beings and who wielded great illusion in battle."

sanskrit: dattvā puṇyām imāṃ vīra saumyām abhayadakṣiṇām diṣṭyā vardhasi kākutstha jayenāmitrakarśana
english: "Having bestowed this auspicious and gracious gift of fearlessness, by good fortune you prosper, O Kākutstha, O crusher of foes, through your victory."

sanskrit: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā rāmaḥ prāñjalir abravīt
english: Having heard the words of those purified-souled sages, Rāma was filled with the greatest wonder and, with joined palms, spoke.

sanskrit: bhavantaḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ ca niśācaram atikramya mahāvīryau kiṃ praśaṃsatha rāvaṇim
english: "Why do you, sirs, passing over Kumbhakarṇa and Rāvaṇa the night-wanderer, both of tremendous might, praise Rāvaṇa's son?"

sanskrit: mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca virūpākṣaṃ ca rākṣasaṃ atikramya mahāvīryān kiṃ praśaṃsatha rāvaṇim
english: "Passing over Mahodara, Prahasta, and the rākṣasa Virūpākṣa — all of tremendous might — why do you praise Rāvaṇa's son?"

sanskrit: kīdṛśo vai prabhāvo 'sya kiṃ balaṃ kaḥ parākramaḥ kena vā kāraṇenaiṣa rāvaṇād atiricyate
english: "What was his power, what his strength, what his valor? And for what reason did he surpass Rāvaṇa himself?"

sanskrit: śakyaṃ yadi mayā śrotuṃ na khalv ājñāpayāmi vaḥ yadi guhyaṃ na ced vaktuṃ śrotum icchāmi kathyatām kathaṃ śakro jitas tena kathaṃ labdhavaraś ca saḥ
english: "If it is possible for me to hear this, I do not command you — if it is not a secret, then tell it, for I desire to hear. How was Indra conquered by him, and how did he obtain his boons?"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ kumbhayonir mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: Having heard these words of the great-souled Rāghava, Kumbhayoni — Agastya, of great brilliance — spoke these words.

sanskrit: śṛṇu rājan yathāvṛttaṃ yasya tejobalaṃ mahat jaghāna ca ripūn yuddhe yathāvadhyaś ca śatrubhiḥ
english: "Hear, O king, the full account of him whose fiery power was great, who slew his enemies in battle, and how he was unkillable by his foes."

sanskrit: ahaṃ te rāvaṇasyedaṃ kulaṃ janma ca rāghava varapradānaṃ ca tathā tasmai dattaṃ bravīmi te
english: "I shall tell you, O Rāghava, Rāvaṇa's lineage and birth, and likewise the grant of boons that was given to him."

sanskrit: purā kṛtayuge rāma prajāpatisutaḥ prabhuḥ pulastyo nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣād iva pitāmahaḥ
english: "In former times, in the Kṛta age, O Rāma, there was a lord who was the son of Prajāpati — the brahmarṣi named Pulastya, like Brahma himself made manifest."

sanskrit: nānukīrtyā guṇās tasya dharmataḥ śīlatas tathā prajāpateḥ putra iti vaktuṃ śakyaṃ hi nāmataḥ
english: "His virtues in respect of righteousness and conduct cannot be enumerated; he can only be described by name as 'son of Prajāpati.'"

sanskrit: sa tu dharmaprasaṅgena meroḥ pārśve mahāgireḥ tṛṇabindvāśramaṃ gatvā nyavasan munipuṃgavaḥ
english: "That foremost of sages, drawn by religious engagement, went to the hermitage of Tṛṇabindu on the slope of the great mountain Meru and dwelt there."

sanskrit: tapas tepe sa dharmātmā svādhyāyaniyatendriyaḥ gatvāśramapadaṃ tasya vighnaṃ kurvanti kanyakāḥ
english: "That righteous-souled sage practiced austerities with his senses restrained through recitation of the Vedas; yet maidens coming to his hermitage created disturbances."

sanskrit: devapannagakanyāś ca rājarṣitanayāś ca yāḥ krīḍantyo 'psarasaś caiva taṃ deśam upapedire
english: "Daughters of gods and nāgas, daughters of royal sages, and apsarases at play — all these came to that region."

sanskrit: sarvartuṣūpabhogyatvād ramyatvāt kānanasya ca nityaśas tās tu taṃ deśaṃ gatvā krīḍanti kanyakāḥ
english: "Because the forest was enjoyable in every season and delightful, those maidens went to that region constantly to sport."

sanskrit: atha ruṣṭo mahātejā vyājahāra mahāmuniḥ yā me darśanam āgacchet sā garbhaṃ dhārayiṣyati
english: "Then the great sage, blazing with might, became angered and proclaimed: 'Whatever woman comes into my sight shall bear a child.'"

sanskrit: tās tu sarvāḥ pratigatāḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ mahātmanaḥ brahmaśāpabhayād bhītās taṃ deśaṃ nopacakramuḥ
english: "All of them, having heard the word of the great-souled one, turned back; fearing a brahmin's curse, they did not approach that region."

sanskrit: tṛṇabindos tu rājarṣes tanayā na śṛṇoti tat gatvāśramapadaṃ tasya vicacāra sunirbhayā
english: "But the daughter of the royal sage Tṛṇabindu did not hear this; she went to his hermitage and wandered there quite without fear."

sanskrit: tasminn eva tu kāle sa prājāpatyo mahān ṛṣiḥ svādhyāyam akarot tatra tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ
english: "At that very time that great sage, son of Prajāpati, was performing his Vedic recitation there, his brilliance blazing with ascetic power."

sanskrit: sā tu vedadhvaniṃ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā caiva tapodhanam abhavat pāṇḍudehā sā suvyañjitaśarīrajā
english: "She, hearing the sound of the Vedas and seeing that treasury of austerities, became pale in her body, though she was a woman of well-formed limbs."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā paramasaṃvignā sā tu tadrūpam ātmanaḥ idaṃ me kiṃ nv iti jñātvā pitur gatvāgrataḥ sthitā
english: "Seeing her own form in such a state, she was greatly agitated; thinking 'What is this that has happened to me?' she went and stood before her father."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā tathā bhūtāṃ tṛṇabindur athābravīt kiṃ tvam etat tv asadṛśaṃ dhārayasy ātmano vapuḥ
english: "Tṛṇabindu, seeing her in that condition, then said: 'Why do you bear this form so unlike your own?'"

sanskrit: sā tu kṛtvāñjaliṃ dīnā kanyovāca tapodhanam na jāne kāraṇaṃ tāta yena me rūpam īdṛśam
english: "She, distressed, joined her palms and said to that treasury of austerities: 'I do not know the cause, father, by which my form has become like this.'"

sanskrit: kiṃ tu pūrvaṃ gatāsmy ekā maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ pulastyasyāśramaṃ divyam anveṣṭuṃ svasakhījanam
english: "'But earlier I had gone alone to the divine hermitage of the great sage Pulastya, whose soul was purified, in search of my own companions.'"

sanskrit: na ca paśyāmy ahaṃ tatra kāṃ cid apy āgatāṃ sakhīm rūpasya tu viparyāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā cāham ihāgatā
english: "'I did not see any companion who had come there; and seeing the transformation of my form, I have come back here.'"

sanskrit: tṛṇabindus tu rājarṣis tapasā dyotitaprabhaḥ dhyānaṃ viveśa tac cāpi apaśyad ṛṣikarmajam
english: "The royal sage Tṛṇabindu, his brilliance blazing with austerity, entered into meditation and saw therein what had come about through the sage's act."

sanskrit: sa tu vijñāya taṃ śāpaṃ maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ gṛhītvā tanayāṃ gatvā pulastyam idam abravīt
english: "Having understood that curse of the great purified-souled sage, he took his daughter and went to Pulastya and said this."

sanskrit: bhagavaṃs tanayāṃ me tvaṃ guṇaiḥ svair eva bhūṣitām bhikṣāṃ pratigṛhāṇemāṃ maharṣe svayam udyatām
english: "'Venerable one, accept this daughter of mine, herself adorned with her own virtues, as a gift, O great sage — she offers herself willingly.'"

sanskrit: tapaścaraṇayuktasya śrāmyamāṇendriyasya te śuśrūṣātatparā nityaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "'She will always be devoted to your service as you practice your austerities and fatigue your senses — of this there is no doubt.'"

sanskrit: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājarṣiṃ dhārmikaṃ tadā jighṛkṣur abravīt kanyāṃ bāḍham ity eva sa dvijaḥ
english: "As the righteous royal sage spoke those words, the brahmin, wishing to accept the maiden, said simply 'So be it.'"

sanskrit: dattvā tu sa gato rājā svam āśramapadaṃ tadā sāpi tatrāvasat kanyā toṣayantī patiṃ guṇaiḥ prītaḥ sa tu mahātejā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: "Having given her, the king departed to his own hermitage; and the maiden dwelt there, pleasing her husband with her virtues. Delighted, that blazing sage spoke these words."

sanskrit: parituṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te guṇānāṃ saṃpadā bhṛśam tasmāt te viramāmy adya putram ātmasamaṃ guṇaiḥ ubhayor vaṃśakartāraṃ paulastya iti viśrutam
english: "'I am thoroughly pleased; may good come to you through the abundance of your virtues. Therefore I shall now produce for you a son equal to me in qualities, who shall perpetuate the lineage of us both, renowned as a son of Pulastya.'"

sanskrit: yasmāt tu viśruto vedas tvayehābhyasyato mama tasmāt sa viśravā nāma bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "'Since the Veda has become famous through being recited by you here in my presence, therefore the son shall be named Viśravas — of this there is no doubt.'"

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā kanyā prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā acireṇaiva kālena sūtā viśravasaṃ sutam
english: "Thus addressed, the maiden, with a joyful heart, in no long time gave birth to a son, Viśravas."

sanskrit: sa tu lokatraye khyātaḥ śaucadharmasamanvitaḥ piteva tapasā yukto viśravā munipuṃgavaḥ
english: "He, renowned through the three worlds, endowed with purity and righteousness, yoked to austerity like his father — Viśravas, that foremost of sages."

sanskrit: atha putraḥ pulastyasya viśravā munipuṃgavaḥ acireṇaiva kālena piteva tapasi sthitaḥ
english: Now Pulastya's son Viśravas, that foremost of sages, in no long time was established in austerity just like his father.

sanskrit: satyavāñ śīlavān dakṣaḥ svādhyāyanirataḥ śuciḥ sarvabhogeṣv asaṃsakto nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: He was truthful, virtuous, capable, devoted to Vedic recitation, pure, unattached to all pleasures, and ever intent on righteousness.

sanskrit: jñātvā tasya tu tadvṛttaṃ bharadvājo mahān ṛṣiḥ dadau viśravase bhāryāṃ svāṃ sutāṃ devavarṇinīm
english: The great sage Bharadvāja, knowing his conduct and character, gave his own daughter to Viśravas as a wife — a woman of divine beauty.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu dharmeṇa bharadvājasutāṃ tadā mudā paramayā yukto viśravā munipuṃgavaḥ
english: Accepting Bharadvāja's daughter in accordance with dharma, Viśravas, that foremost of sages, was filled with the greatest joy.

sanskrit: sa tasyāṃ vīryasaṃpannam apatyaṃ paramādbhutam janayām āsa dharmātmā sarvair brahmaguṇair yutam
english: That righteous-souled one begot upon her a most wondrous offspring endowed with valor and possessed of all the qualities of a brahmin.

sanskrit: tasmiñ jāte tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ sa babhūva pitāmahaḥ nāma cāsyākarot prītaḥ sārdhaṃ devarṣibhis tadā
english: At his birth, the Grandfather Brahmā was greatly delighted, and in joy he gave the child his name together with the divine sages at that time.

sanskrit: yasmād viśravaso 'patyaṃ sādṛśyād viśravā iva tasmād vaiśravaṇo nāma bhaviṣyaty eṣa viśrutaḥ
english: "Since this is the offspring of Viśravas and resembles Viśravas himself, therefore shall he be renowned by the name Vaiśravaṇa."

sanskrit: sa tu vaiśravaṇas tatra tapovanagatas tadā avardhata mahātejā hutāhutir ivānalaḥ
english: And Vaiśravaṇa, having gone to the forest of austerities, grew there blazing with great splendor like fire fed with oblations.

sanskrit: tasyāśramapadasthasya buddhir jajñe mahātmanaḥ cariṣye niyato dharmaṃ dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ
english: Dwelling at his hermitage, this thought arose in the great-souled one's mind: "I shall follow dharma with self-restraint, for dharma is the highest path."

sanskrit: sa tu varṣasahasrāṇi tapas taptvā mahāvane pūrṇe varṣasahasre tu taṃ taṃ vidhim avartata
english: He practiced austerities in the great forest for thousands of years, and at the completion of each thousand years he observed the prescribed rites in their succession.

sanskrit: jalāśī mārutāhāro nirāhāras tathaiva ca evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi jagmus tāny eva varṣavat
english: Living on water alone, then subsisting on air alone, then taking no sustenance at all — in this manner those thousands of years passed as though they were so many rainy seasons.

sanskrit: atha prīto mahātejāḥ sendraiḥ suragaṇaiḥ saha gatvā tasyāśramapadaṃ brahmedaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Brahmā, greatly pleased, went together with the host of gods led by Indra to his hermitage and spoke these words.

sanskrit: parituṣṭo 'smi te vatsa karmaṇānena suvrata varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te varārhas tvaṃ hi me mataḥ
english: "I am thoroughly pleased with this conduct of yours, O dear child, O one of good vows. Choose a boon — may good come to you, for you are worthy of a boon in my estimation."

sanskrit: athābravīd vaiśravaṇaḥ pitāmaham upasthitam bhagavaṃl lokapālatvam iccheyaṃ vittarakṣaṇam
english: Then Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Grandfather who stood before him: "Venerable one, I desire the guardianship of a world and the protection of wealth."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd vaiśravaṇaṃ parituṣṭena cetasā brahmā suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ bāḍham ity eva hṛṣṭavat
english: Then Brahmā, with a thoroughly pleased heart, said to Vaiśravaṇa together with the host of gods, joyfully: "So be it."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi lokapālānāṃ caturthaṃ sraṣṭum udyataḥ yamendravaruṇānāṃ hi padaṃ yat tava cepsitam
english: "I am indeed prepared to create a fourth guardian of the worlds, for the position alongside Yama, Indra, and Varuṇa is precisely what you desire."

sanskrit: tatkṛtaṃ gaccha dharmajña dhaneśatvam avāpnuhi yamendravaruṇānāṃ hi caturtho 'dya bhaviṣyasi
english: "So it is done — go, O knower of dharma, and obtain lordship over wealth; you shall henceforth be the fourth alongside Yama, Indra, and Varuṇa."

sanskrit: etac ca puṣpakaṃ nāma vimānaṃ sūryasaṃnibham pratigṛhṇīṣva yānārthaṃ tridaśaiḥ samatāṃ vraja
english: "And accept this celestial vehicle named Puṣpaka, brilliant as the sun, for your conveyance; proceed to equality with the thirty gods."

sanskrit: svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmaḥ sarva eva yathāgatam kṛtakṛtyā vayaṃ tāta dattvā tava mahāvaram
english: "May all go well with you; we shall all depart as we came, our purpose fulfilled, dear child, having bestowed upon you this great boon."

sanskrit: gateṣu brahmapūrveṣu deveṣv atha nabhastalam dhaneśaḥ pitaraṃ prāha vinayāt praṇato vacaḥ
english: When Brahmā and the gods before him had departed to the sky, the lord of wealth humbly bowed and spoke these words to his father.

sanskrit: bhagavaṃl labdhavān asmi varaṃ kamalayonitaḥ nivāsaṃ na tu me devo vidadhe sa prajāpatiḥ
english: "Venerable father, I have received a boon from the lotus-born Brahmā, but that Prajāpati has not ordained a dwelling place for me."

sanskrit: tat paśya bhagavan kaṃ cid deśaṃ vāsāya naḥ prabho na ca pīḍā bhaved yatra prāṇino yasya kasya cit
english: "Therefore, venerable lord, look out some region for our dwelling — one where no living creature of any kind would be distressed."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu putreṇa viśravā munipuṃgavaḥ vacanaṃ prāha dharmajña śrūyatām iti dharmavit
english: Thus addressed by his son, Viśravas, that foremost of sages and knower of dharma, said: "O knower of dharma, hear these words."

sanskrit: laṅkā nāma purī ramyā nirmitā viśvakarmaṇā rākṣasānāṃ nivāsārthaṃ yathendrasyāmarāvatī
english: "There is a beautiful city named Laṅkā, built by Viśvakarman for the dwelling of the rākṣasas, like Amarāvatī for Indra."

sanskrit: ramaṇīyā purī sā hi rukmavaidūryatoraṇā rākṣasaiḥ sā parityaktā purā viṣṇubhayārditaiḥ śūnyā rakṣogaṇaiḥ sarvai rasātalatalaṃ gataiḥ
english: "That delightful city has archways of gold and vaidūrya; it was abandoned long ago by the rākṣasas who were tormented by fear of Viṣṇu, left empty of all the hosts of rākṣasas who had gone down to the depths of the underworld."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ tatra nivāsāya rocayasva matiṃ svakām nirdoṣas tatra te vāso na ca bādhāsti kasya cit
english: "Direct your own mind toward dwelling there; your residence there shall be without fault, and no one shall be harmed."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu dharmātmā dharmiṣṭhaṃ vacanaṃ pituḥ niveśayām āsa tadā laṅkāṃ parvatamūrdhani
english: Hearing his father's most righteous counsel, that righteous-souled one then established himself in Laṅkā on the mountain summit.

sanskrit: nairṛtānāṃ sahasrais tu hṛṣṭaiḥ pramuditaiḥ sadā acireṇaikakālena saṃpūrṇā tasya śāsanāt
english: By his command, that city was speedily filled with thousands of joyful and ever-rejoicing nairṛtas — the rākṣasa folk.

sanskrit: atha tatrāvasat prīto dharmātmā nairṛtādhipaḥ samudraparidhānāyāṃ laṅkāyāṃ viśravātmajaḥ
english: And there dwelt with delight that righteous-souled lord of the nairṛtas, the son of Viśravas, in Laṅkā girdled by the ocean.

sanskrit: kāle kāle vinītātmā puṣpakeṇa dhaneśvaraḥ abhyagacchat susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca saḥ
english: Season after season, humble in spirit, the lord of wealth joyfully came on the Puṣpaka vehicle to visit both his father and his mother.

sanskrit: sa devagandharvagaṇair abhiṣṭutas tathaiva siddhaiḥ saha cāraṇair api gabhastibhiḥ sūrya ivaujasā vṛtaḥ pituḥ samīpaṃ prayayau śriyā vṛtaḥ
english: Praised by hosts of gods and gandharvas, and likewise by siddhas along with cāraṇas, surrounded by his own radiance like the sun encircled by his rays, he proceeded to his father's presence attended by all prosperity.
